incident-bot: [PAGE] 1901300000 - gpu-vram-pressure rack-4: multiple OOMKills & node drains detected. Paging @Maya

Maya (oncall): I'm awake. seeing repeated OOMKills and pods entering CrashLoopBackOff on nodes gpu-40..gpu-43. Starting triage.

Leo (eng-sre): Can you paste the `kubectl get nodes` and a sample `dmesg | tail -n 50` from one affected host? Also want to see `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu --format=csv`

Maya (oncall): from gpu-42:
```
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu --format=csv
memory.used [MiB], memory.total [MiB], utilization.gpu [%], temperature.gpu []
15360 MiB, 16384 MiB, 99 %, 85
```
`dmesg` excerpts show repeated GPU driver OOM notifier entries and rmmalloc failures.

Priya (infra): rack-4 cooling report shows a transient drop in chilled-air supply at 02:12 (local), which correlates with temp rise. We'll spin up extra fans and run the CRAC boost.

Carmen (eng-runtime): Were there any large model rollouts or batch size changes? Checking deployments... I see a canary push to inference-service with larger batch_size at 01:55 UTC. It targeted a subset of pods.

Maya (oncall): that might explain sustained VRAM pressure. The runtime should have autoscale/batching limits but looks like the canary misconfigured a batch_size=64.

Leo (eng-sre): Immediate mitigation plan:
- 1) Stop the canary: rollback the batch_size change and roll back to previous config.
- 2) Cordons for affected nodes to prevent new pods scheduling: `kubectl cordon gpu-40 gpu-41 gpu-42 gpu-43`.
- 3) Evict only non-ml-system pods gracefully, avoid mass drains until we snapshot caches.

Maya (oncall): executing rollback now. `kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-service --to-revision=3` 

deploy-bot: rollout undo started for inference-service -> revision 3.

Carmen (eng-runtime): rollback in progress. I'll also patch the autoscaler to cap max_batch: 16 while we investigate.

Zoe (observability): Dashboard shows VRAM utilization spike starting 01:58 and peaking 02:05. OOMKill count per-pod increased between 02:02-02:10. Linking graph: https://observability.internal/d/XYZ/gpu-vram?from=now-2h

Anika (customer-success): Seeing a handful of customer 5xxs - mostly short-lived. Any idea on numbers?

Maya (oncall): preliminary: ~0.03% of requests impacted, concentrated to tenant T-422 and T-987 during the spike. I'll hold a customer note draft but will wait for RCA.

Leo (eng-sre): For immediate alerting noise control, I'll apply a 20m suppression to the GPU_VRAM_CRIT pager but keep the node-drain PD alive. Use: `/pagerduty suppress GPU_VRAM_CRIT 20m reason:"mitigating misconfig rollback"`

ops-bot: suppression applied to GPU_VRAM_CRIT for 20m by Leo.

Maya (oncall): cordon done. Taking one node at a time to drain; snapshotting KV caches first to reduce cold-start cost.

Carmen (eng-runtime): Confirmed that rollback reduces per-pod memory footprint. New pods are starting with earlier config.

Priya (infra): cooling boost applied. temperatures start dropping: gpu temps down to ~73C in 10 minutes.

Leo (eng-sre): Post-incident monitoring / alert tuning proposals (to avoid repeats):
- GPU_VRAM_Utilization_Current (fires now on >90% on any GPU) -> change to: trigger when avg_over_time(gpu_memory_used_bytes/gpu_memory_total_bytes[10m]) > 0.90 for 5m and increase only if pod_ooms > 0 or node_evictions > 0. Rationale: avoid paging on single short allocation spikes.
- Add a new composite alert: GPU_BURST_VRAM_WITH_OOM which requires both sustained high VRAM and increase(node_pod_oom_total[10m]) > 0. This one should page PD.
- Cluster-level anomaly: if >2 nodes in same rack exceed 85% VRAM concurrently for >7m then alert to eng-sre (not PD) first, escalate to PD if evictions happen.
- Add a soft warning Slack channel #eng-runtime-warnings for 80-90% VRAM events with sample tenants and pod names. Keep PD for >90%+ooms.

Leo (eng-sre): I'll open monitoring PR with examples and tests. PR: https://git.internal/infra/monitoring/pulls/254

Zoe (observability): I'll add a per-pod VRAM histogram panel and a per-rack aggregation tile plus an annotation for recent rollouts (so we can correlate config changes to spikes). ETA: 3 hours. Ticket MON-577.

Carmen (eng-runtime): Also adding runtime safeguard: reject batch_size > 32 for now in admission webhook and log the attempted change. I'll add a feature flag to allow controlled increases after perf validation.

Maya (oncall): timeline notes for incident doc:
- 01:55 UTC - canary with increased batch_size deployed to subset of inference pods
- 01:58 - VRAM utilization climbs on rack-4 nodes
- 02:02 - first OOMKill observed on pod inference-xyz-7
- 02:04 - incident-bot alert triggered for VRAM pressure
- 02:10 - rollback initiated and cordon started
- 02:18 - cooling boost applied
- 02:30 - nodes stabilized, workloads redistributed

Maya (oncall): assigning follow-ups:
- Leo: monitoring rule PR + grouping changes. (#MON-254)
- Zoe: dashboard panels + rollout annotation. (MON-577)
- Priya: hardware/cooling verification & rack inspection. (HW-340)
- Carmen: runtime admission limit + webhook tests. (RT-116)
- Maya: incident writeup + customer impact note. (INC-911)

Anika (customer-success): I'll prepare a short customer-safe line: "We briefly experienced GPU memory saturation in a subset of nodes due to a misconfigured canary. Workloads were automatically redistributed and retries handled most requests; a small number of requests were transiently affected." Will hold until doc published.

Maya (oncall): lifting suppression at 02:40 if steady; keeping nodes cordoned until HW check completes. Scheduling RCA at 15:00 UTC today.

incident-bot: [INCIDENT RESOLVE] 1901300000 - incident marked resolved. Logs and timeline uploaded to docs: https://docs.internal/incidents/1901300000

Maya (oncall): last_message_ts: 1901304200
